newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat closes higher, rains slow harvest.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat closes higher, rains slow harvest.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed higher, supported mainly by concern about continuing harvest delays in rain-hit North Dakota.
"There is still concern about harvest delays up in North Dakota and with the rains today it just emphasized that," one dealer said.
They noted, however, that drier weather was forecast for the rest of the week, which should aid harvest progress.
September rose to its highest level for two months, peaking at $4.06 a bushel and closed up 5-3/4 cents at $4.04-3/4. Other months were 5-1/2 to two cents higher.

Floor sources said Atwood and Continental Grain each bought 1.0 million bushels of September while Country Hedging sold 1.2 million bushels of September and 700,000 bushels of December. Prudential Securities sold 1.1 million December.
Atwood also bull spread 1.0 million bushels of Sep/Dec at between three and four cents with General Mills taking the other side of the spread.
Estimated volume on spring wheat totalled 30.4 million bushels, up from 26.0 million on Monday.
